implementation_constraints: reads one JSON value from stdin, prints one line, exits 0

unresolved_intent.ir_region: Contract — 'JSON array of known event strings'
unresolved_intent.decision: validation is per-element and short-circuits: the fold stops and prints ERROR at the first invalid element rather than scanning the whole array first
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec states the error condition per-element ('if an array element is...') without mandating whole-array pre-validation before folding; short-circuit is the simpler reading and matches 'fold from left to right'

unresolved_intent.ir_region: Errors — 'is not a JSON object, a bare number, or invalid JSON'
unresolved_intent.decision: treated JSON true/false/null as also erroring (falls under 'not a JSON array'), even though the spec's error list names object/number/invalid-JSON explicitly but not boolean/null
unresolved_intent.rationale: the Contract clause is the controlling rule ('when the input is not a JSON array... print ERROR'); the Errors bullet's enumeration reads as illustrative examples, not an exhaustive type list, so any non-array top-level value is treated the same

unresolved_intent.decision: a JSON boolean (true/false) or null or nested array/object as an array element is treated as 'not a string' and prints ERROR, not specially distinguished from other non-string types
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec only distinguishes 'unknown event' (wrong string) from 'not a string' (wrong type); both paths in the code print the same literal ERROR so no further type discrimination is needed

unresolved_intent.ir_region: Transitions — self-loop wording ('the program shall keep the state')
unresolved_intent.decision: implemented as an explicit if/else assignment to the same value (state = 'unlocked' when already 'unlocked') rather than a no-op/pass, to keep the total 2x2 transition table visually explicit in code
unresolved_intent.rationale: the constitution (INV-SM-TOTAL-01) demands the machine be visibly total and closed; writing all four transitions explicitly (even where redundant) makes totality auditable in the source rather than relying on an implicit fallthrough

unresolved_intent.ir_region: Contract — 'read one JSON value from standard input'
unresolved_intent.decision: read the ENTIRE stdin stream with sys.stdin.read() and parse it as a single JSON document, rather than reading only the first line or first JSON token
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec says 'one JSON value', which may be pretty-printed/multi-line; reading all of stdin and parsing once is the standard way to accept a single JSON value regardless of formatting
